Here is an introduction to Good Documentation.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you will be able to:

- Explain why good documentation is worth developing
- Describe the different ways in which code can be documented
- Understand the major features of good documentation

## Prerequisites


## What is documentation?

- Code annotation
- Vignettes
- Formal help files
- READMEs
- Contribution guides? Higher level

## Why do we need good documentation?
- Convert the skeptics, why is this a good use of time?
- How-to for people who are already keen

## Topics to include

Talk about the philosophy, who is your audience and how can you give them what they need to know?

Do clear object names remove the need for annotation?

Use of simpler English to make it more understandable, helps with translation also 

People using AI as a shortcut to generating documentation, what does this risk? Better for ‘what’ than ‘why’, this is more or less relevant for different elements of the documentation

How to select examples, vignette topics

Code annotation
Structure

Good documentation is essential for code reuse, and helpful for review - hard to evaluate what is sufficient, or what the payoff could or would be

Link to other modules on rmarkdown, etc

## Potential exercises

- Poorly documented function, review issues
- Provide a line of documentation, multiple choice on which code line it describes (use the ‘reveal’ option on the website)
- High-level exercise on writing documentation for provided code?

We need examples of good documentation to share!
